one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-12) probably contains the Q3 2026 report: not yet announced, but Q2 came on Aug 12 with the date set ~3 weeks earlier, so mid-November is likely. That would be the first print since the unconfirmed SemiAnalysis/CNBC report that OpenAI's Ultrafast tier runs on Nvidia [4,21,24]. Guidance is core revenue $214-216M, core GM 38-40%, core op margin -23% to -25% [2]. The questions are OpenAI cloud revenue and whether management repeats 'more than triple in 2027'. A bad answer on either could cost 15-25% (the stock fell 16% after hours on the Q2 report [23]). Locked-up supply keeps coming: tranches of up to 14.6M shares every two weeks, 19.4M on Sep 30 [5], and the main lock-up ends around mid-November [13]. The 12.85% short float [11] and the drop from $206.75 to $148.86 since Sep 25 make a relief rally on a clean print possible. I net these to a slightly negative median ($147 vs $148.86) and use a 24% one-month log-sd: an assumed forward vol of ~85% (realized 115% is inflated by the IPO) / 3.5, with the earnings event included.

fair_value.method: 30% DCF (FY2026-29 explicit, 14.9% WACC, 15x FY2029 EBITDA exit) = $102.94; 70% horizon EV/NTM sales of 7.5x (mix-weighted peer P/S: cloud ~4.9x, chip ~13.4x) on ~$3.9B NTM revenue plus net cash = $137.00. Blend $126.78 on ~249M shares at the horizon.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 7.5x NTM EV/sales: below the 11.5x full-set median, inside the range, between the cloud names (CRWV 2.2x, NBIS 7.65x) and the chip/hardware names (median 13.35x). P/E is not meaningful: GAAP losses, and consensus 2027 adj. EPS of only $1.27 [10].
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount to the full-set median reflects structural features that will last through the horizon, not sentiment. (1) Mix: cloud/services was 70% of Q2 GAAP revenue ($126.0M of $180.1M) and the $25.4B RPO is mostly OpenAI inference capacity [1]. That is capex-heavy cloud revenue: 6M capex was 147% of revenue [1], and Q1 capex was 68% of revenue vs ~5-8% for AMD/NVDA [19]. (2) Margins: FY2026 core GM is guided at 41-43% [2] and fell on rented capacity [23], below the chip peers. (3) Concentration: OpenAI is 'essentially all' of backlog [14], and the 10-Q lets the $918M loan accelerate if the MRA ends [1]. Weighting the sub-group multiples by revenue mix gives ~7.0x. I add +0.5x for own silicon and faster NTM growth, net of the long-dated risks below (worth about -$14/share, or -0.9x).

thesis_break_reason: At ~$90 the market cap is ~$21B and EV ~$15-16B after ~$5B of horizon net cash. That is ~4x my ~$3.9B NTM revenue, the neocloud multiple. Trading there would most likely mean the OpenAI ramp is being cut or re-timed (RPO conversion failing, capacity under-used after the Ultrafast routing) or margins are breaking below guidance. Ordinary post-IPO volatility would not explain it. It is also near my bear scenario ($79).

reverse_dcf_check: The engine prices my explicit cash flows with the 7.5x NTM EV/sales multiple and finds it implies a 5.1% WACC, against the 14.9% I build from rf 5.24% + beta 2.29 x ERP 4.20%. My DCF at 14.9% gives $102.94 vs $137.00 for the multiple. So even a multiple at the low end of the peer range assumes much better economics after 2029 than my set: GAAP EBIT margin well above 16%, capex falling from 25% of revenue toward D&A, and the OpenAI capacity renewed past the MRA term. Those are plausible only if own-silicon inference keeps a speed premium, which the long-dated risks above call into question. That is why the DCF carries 30% weight and the multiple sits below the peer median.

sbc_treatment.note: FY2025 SBC $49.8M (S-1/A). 6M 2026 SBC $386.6M (Q2 $377.0M, IPO-related RSU vesting). EBIT is GAAP after SBC (-85% margin in FY2026), so share growth only reflects customer warrants (+3.5%/yr). Revenue is on the core basis, before warrant amortisation ($44.3M in Q2), so the warrants are counted once, in the share count. Peer P/S multiples do not depend on the SBC basis.

defense_exposure.share_of_revenue: Not separately disclosed. No defense, military or intelligence customer is among the >=10% customers. Upper bound: <=14% in FY2025 and <=21% in 6M 2026; likely far lower.
defense_exposure.detail: FY2025: G42 (Abu Dhabi AI/cloud company) 24.0% + MBZUAI (university) 62.0% = 86% from civilian UAE entities [3]. 6M 2026: Customer A 49% + related Customer D 10% (UAE related parties) + Customer B 20% (matches OpenAI's $74.4M of $373.5M) = 79% civilian [1]. The S-1/A lists 'national laboratories, and defense organizations' among target on-prem customers [3]. EDGAR full-text search finds 'Department of Defense' in the S-1/424B4, but I could not read that passage, so no revenue figure is attached.

reasoning: Start from the facts. CBRS is at $148.86, a ~$35B market cap and ~$28.8B EV [11], down 61% from its $386 high. The company is loss-making: 6M 2026 GAAP operating loss was -$492M on $373.5M revenue, and capex was 147% of revenue [1]. It depends on one counterparty: OpenAI is customer, lender ($918M loan), warrant holder, and source of 'essentially all' of the $25.4B backlog [1,14]. In the bear lane, every finding confirmed a known risk; none was a hidden one. There is no short-seller report and no formal downgrade. The lowest target, Freedom's $209, came with an upgrade [8], and Citi and Mizuho made only small cuts [12]. The new negatives are: (a) the unconfirmed SemiAnalysis/CNBC report that OpenAI's Ultrafast tier runs on Nvidia [4,21,24], which I treat as judgment and use only in scenario weights; (b) margin compression from renting capacity (core GM 46.5% -> 40.6%) [23,20] and long per-MW payback [19]; (c) heavy insider and lock-up supply [5,15,22,13]; (d) accounting and governance flags: material weaknesses, a non-cash-driven 2025 GAAP profit, 99.2% Class B voting [3,17]; (e) technology limits on large models [14,7]; (f) OpenAI's own funding gap [9]. Against these: $7.0B net cash plus an undrawn $850M revolver [1,16], guidance raised to $880-890M, management's 'more than triple in 2027' [2], consensus 2027 revenue of $2.95B [10], and 12.85% short float [11]. I value it at a mix-weighted 7.5x NTM sales (70%) and a 14.9% WACC DCF (30%): $126.78, ~15% below spot. Scenarios are $79 / $127 / $194 at 28/50/22%, with a 50% within-scenario log-sd. That gives an implied ~65-70% total vol, below the IPO-inflated 115% realized. The ladder's median is ~$122 and P(>=$149) = 0.37. Research was ~25 searches and fetches. sec.gov blocked script access, so I read filings with WebFetch. Risk-factor pages of the 10-Qs were beyond the fetch window, and I could not confirm the exact lock-up share count, so it is not used.
